A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 30-page versions of the same BrainGFM study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite formatting changes and section moves.

before.justification: v2 reports original disorder-classification results in Table 1 and experiments on pre-training, prompting, atlas transfer, graph construction, and positional encoding.

after.justification: v3 retains original classification and ablation results, revises several scores, and adds graph-construction comparisons and patient/control attention-attribution maps.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Figure 1(b) now include task/disorder tokens [T/D] during pre-training alongside [A/P]. v2 places their introduction at downstream adaptation. This revises the reported conditioning procedure; the backbone, losses, graph prompts, and meta-learning algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Tables 16–17 and 19 retain the datasets, configured classification tasks, and eight parcellations. The new attention analysis uses existing ABIDE/HBN coverage. Table 18 drops an IED taxonomy entry, but the task roster in Table 17 is unchanged; removing ABIDE scores from Table 3 does not remove ABIDE from evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains Pearson top-k and KNN construction for HBN/MDD and adds partial correlation, mutual information, and dynamic connectivity as evaluated alternatives. The main Table 1 comparator set and the other tuning and positional-encoding comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added Table 3 comparisons introduce three alternative connectivity constructions, and Appendix U introduces patient/control comparisons using attention averaged within each group. The retained classification metrics, dataset partitions, training budgets, and backbone sizes are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix U examines learned attention patterns for ASD and MDD patients versus controls. Table 3 broadens graph-construction sensitivity testing on HBN but removes the corresponding ABIDE comparison. The existing prompting, atlas-transfer, tuning, and positional-encoding analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices, including Table 1's ± values and existing plot error bars. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces BrainGFM's ADHD accuracy of 72.2 with 70.5, reversing its reported lead over Brain-JEPA's unchanged 71.6. Its ADNI accuracy changes from 85.1 to 81.9 and HBN/MDD accuracy from 85.5 to 82.0; several baseline values also change. Table 3 adds three results and removes two ABIDE entries, while Figure 10 adds qualitative attribution findings.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, positional encodings, padded-input attention equations, meta-learning updates, Algorithm 1, and reconstruction/contrastive losses in Appendices H–N are mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or formal derivation appears.

C1.justification: The title moderates 'Any Atlas and Disorder' to 'across Broad Atlases and Disorders.' The abstract changes 'pre-trained on 27' datasets to 'established on 27,' narrowing its attribution of the full collection to pre-training. The central framework, transfer, and performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix U newly interprets attention differences as meaningful disorder-related subnetworks and preliminary biomarker evidence, and claims they distinguish learned structure from noise or dataset artifacts. The broader-impact and limitations discussions are retained from v2 Appendices U–V and merely moved into main-text Sections 5–6.

D1.justification: Appendix U newly identifies graph-transformer attention as the attribution source and describes averaging within patient/control groups. Existing implementation and preprocessing details remain. Table 14 changes its generic '>5' inner-step guidance row to '5'; Table 12's actual one-step setting is unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 78 works and retain the same related-work positioning, including the comparison with meta-matching. Alphabetizing and reformatting the bibliography do not change its substantive coverage.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title, affiliations, selected methodological sentences, and several headings. It moves broader impact and limitations before the conclusion and adds Appendix U, while retaining most existing prose and section organization.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICLR headers and typography, regroups Figures 2–3 with Table 1, and redraws plot labels and legends in Figures 3–4. Figure 1 gains the pre-training [T/D] token, Table 3 is restructured, Table 18 loses a row, and Figure 10 adds four attribution panels. Most existing visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The additional graph-construction controls and exploratory attention maps broaden the evidence, and the title and abstract better qualify coverage. However, the ABIDE construction comparison is removed, and revised ADHD accuracy remains highlighted as best despite trailing Brain-JEPA. Appendix U also claims to exclude dataset artifacts without an accompanying test. These limited gains and reporting/interpretation problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
